contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 1 — Qualifications and taking office

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to update the qualifications for the offices of mayor and city commissioner, and provide that elected officials assume office at the first regular City Commission meeting following certification of their election, and that a vice mayor be designated at the City Commission’s first meeting after all elected officials assume office following a regular municipal election and annually thereafter, instead of at the first meeting in April?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 2 — Candidate documentation

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to specify the procedure for candidates for the office of mayor or city commissioner to submit documentation to the City Clerk for review?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 3 — Challenges to candidates

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to remove the City Commission’s authority to receive affidavits alleging that a candidate for the office of mayor or city commissioner has violated the Charter or is unqualified and make a finding as to whether such candidate violated the Charter or is unqualified, thereby leaving such considerations to the courts?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 4 — Special-meeting notice

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended so that special meetings of the City Commission may be called upon at least seventy-two hours’ notice, except that in the event of an emergency, where there is the potential for imminent harm or the ability to lessen or avert a catastrophe, a special meeting of the City Commission may be called upon such notice as is practicable under the circumstances?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 5 — Civil Service Board

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to prescribe a method for resolving a tie in nominations to the Civil Service Board Nominating Committee, modify the composition of the Election Board that certifies the results of elections for the classified employees’ recommendation for appointment to the Civil Service Board, and remove the Civil Service Board’s duty to review, consider, and advise the City Manager concerning job class specifications?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 6 — Temporary managers, notices and election wording

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to delete references to primary elections, remove the requirement of two newspaper publications for public hearings and other types of notice, and distinguish the title of interim city manager, who is appointed in the event of the city manager's resignation or termination, from that of acting city manager, who is appointed during temporary absences of the city manager?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 7 — City property sales and use agreements

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to simplify the sale of City-owned personal property such as vehicles, furniture, and equipment, and City-owned land other than parks, to add limitations on lease, license, concession, or other types of use agreements with private parties for the use of City-owned land, and to add limitations on the sale or lease of City-owned land to other governments?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 8 — Park-land use agreements

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to require a unanimous vote of the entire City Commission for any license agreement, concession agreement, facility use agreement, or other type of use agreement for more than one year for the use of City-owned park land?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 9 — Police chief reports to Commission

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to establish the Charter position of Police Chief, who shall report directly to the City Commission rather than to the City Manager, and be employed and compensated under such terms and conditions as the City Commission deems appropriate?

contests.title: Fort Lauderdale Charter Amendment 10 — Fire chief reports to Commission

provenance.quote: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to establish the Charter position of Fire Chief, who shall report directly to the City Commission rather than to the City Manager, and be employed and compensated under such terms and conditions as the City Commission deems appropriate?

SECTION 1. That Section 6.04 of the Charter of the City of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, be, and
is hereby amended to provide as follows:

Sec. 6.04. - Civil service board; created; composition.

(a) Purpose of board. There shall be a civil service board, the members
of which shall be residents and electors of the City of Fort
Lauderdale, who shall be in sympathy with the application of merit
principles in connection with public employment. No member of the
board shall hold or be a candidate for any elective public office.

(b)

Membership; appointment, etc. The civil service board shall consist
of three (3) members, one (1) of whom shall be recommended for
appointment by the mayor, with approval of city commission; one (1)
of whom shall be recommended for appointment by the city manager;
and the third member shall be recommended for appointment by the
regular employees of the City of Fort Lauderdale who are in the
classified service as of May 31 of the year of the appointment. Each
member shall be appointed by resolution for a full term of four (4)
years, which resolution shall specify upon whose recommendation
the member was appointed, and the expiration of his or her term of
office. The present members of the board shall serve until the
expiration of their terms of office or until their successors are
appointed and qualified. If the office is vacated by death, resignation,
removal or other effective cause prior to expiration of the term, the
vacancy shall be filled by appointment by the city commission upon
recommendation of the proper authority, for the balance of the
unexpired term. All regular full terms shall be for a period of four (4)
years from the expiration of the preceding term. Recommendations
for appointment by the mayor and city manager shall be made to the
city commission in writing at least twenty (20) days prior to expiration
of the term of the member whose successor it is the duty of such
Officials, respectively, to recommend for appointment.

Recommendations for appointment by the employees shall be made in the
following manner: At least forty (40) days before expiration of the term of the
member to be filled upon recommendation of civil service employees, civil
service employees shall be notified that for a period of seven (7) days sealed
nominations will be received for members of a nominating committee
representing the civil service employees. Any regular employee in the
classified service shall have the right to nominate any other regular employee
in the classified service as a member of such nominating committee. At the

po ola of seven A days from such notification, ee

the five (5) employees receiving the highest number of yvotes-nominations
shall become the nominating committee to nominate up to three (3)

candidates for the office to be filled. In instances in which there is a tie in
nominations for the nominating committee, the employee(s) with the highest
level of overall City seniority shall serve on the nominating committee. For the
purposes of this section, overall City seniority shall be defined as an
employee’s length of continuous service with the City. Upon vote of the
regular employees in the classified service, the person receiving the highest
number of votes, and otherwise qualified, shall be recommended to the city
commission for appointment. The city manager's designee and two (2) city
cormmissioners—appointed_by_the—mayer—members of the nominating
committee shall constitute the election board and shall certify the results to
the city commission in writing.

No person shall be eligible to be a member of the civil service board who is
an officer or employee of the city or who is serving the city upon an advisory
board or in any other capacity (except as a member of the civil service board),
nor shall the husband or wife of such a person or other relative (as defined
by law) of such a person be eligible for membership.

If, because of lack of sufficient time, or other valid reason, except willful
failure to so do, proper nominations are not made before the expiration of a
term, the incumbent shall hold over until his or her successor is appointed
and qualified, but the term of the new appointee shall run for the balance of
the full four-year term only. If, for any reason the mayor, city manager or
employees of the city should fail to make their respective recommendations
for appointment within sixty (60) days after expiration of a term, the city
commission shall appoint a qualified person to membership upon said board,
whose term shall run for the balance of the unexpired term only.

All members of the board shall file an oath to support and defend the
Constitution of the United States and of the State of Florida, and to faithfully
perform the duties of the office. The members of the board shall elect one (1)
of their members to serve as a chairman for a two-year term.

(c) Duties of the board. The board shall:

(1) Hear appeals as outlined in section 6.04(d).

(2) Review and consider additional personnel rules or
amendments to existing rules that may be recommended for
adoption, and approve or disapprove, by motion, these rules.

(43) Meet at such times and places as shall be required to conduct
the business of the board as outlined in paragraphs (1);_and
(2)-and+3}, above. Time and place of the meeting shall be
specified by the call of the chairman of the board or by a
majority of the board. All meetings shall be open to the public.
Notice of each meeting shall be given in writing to each board

member by the secretary of the board. Two (2) members shall
constitute a quorum for the transaction of business.

(d) Appeals to the board. Regular employees subject to personnel rules
and regulations who are suspended, dismissed or demoted, or who
believe the personnel rules have been improperly applied or
misinterpreted to their detriment, may appeal to the board within
thirty (30) calendar days from the date such action is taken, or from
the date an employee by use of reasonable diligence should have
become aware of the action causing the appeal, and the board shall
hear and take action upon such appeal. Upon such appeal, the
appealing employee and the city management staff shall have the
right to be heard publicly and to present evidence. At the hearing of
such appeal, technical rules of evidence shall not apply. The board
shall make the final decision disposing of the appeal. If such final
decision is in favor of the employee, the city manager shall reinstate
the employee without loss of pay and benefits.

(e) Powers of the board. The board, each member of the board, and the
secretary to the board, who shall be designated by the city manager,
shall have power to administer oaths, subpoena witnesses, and
compel the production of books and papers pertinent to any
investigation or hearing authorized by this charter. Any person who
shall fail to appear in response to a subpoena or to answer any

question or produce any books or papers pertinent to any such
investigation or hearing or who shall knowingly give false testimony

deputy city manager, assistant city manager, or department director to

temporarily exercise the powers and duties of the city manager. The person
thus designated shall be known as "acting city manager."

SECTION 2. That Section 4.08 of the Charter of the City of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, be, and
is hereby amended to provide as follows:

Sec. 4.08. - Removal or discharge.

The city manager may be removed or discharged by resolution of the city
commission at any time. In such resolution the commission shall designate
an aeting-interim_ city manager to serve in the place of the removed city
manager, and the removed city manager shall vacate the office upon
adoption of the resolution. Within five (5) days after the adoption of
resolution removing or discharging him or her, such removed city manager
shall have the right to have served upon him or her written statement of
specific reasons for his or her discharge, if he or she so desires, by filing a
demand for same with the city clerk, and leaving sufficient copies with the
city clerk for service upon members of the city.commission. Such written
statement of specific reasons, signed by a majority of the city commission
shall be delivered to such removed officer within five (5) days after service
of such demand as aforesaid, and a definite time and date fixed in such
written statement for a public hearing before the commission within not less
than five (5) days and not more than ten (10) days after the service of such
written statement. At the time and place specified the city commission shall
convene as a body at a special meeting for the purpose of conducting a
public hearing upon such charges. The removed city manager shall have
the right to appear at such hearing to answer and rebut such charges or
reasons, and he or she shall have the right to be represented by his or her
own private counsel. At the conclusion of such hearing the commission shall
adopt a resolution confirming such removal or reinstating such removed city
manager. If reinstated he or she shall receive full pay for the period
intervening between his or her removal and reinstatement.

An acting-interim city manager may be removed at any time by resolution
of the city commission, and such removed person shall not be entitled to a
public hearing upon such removal.

SECTION 3. That Section 6.02 of the Charter of the City of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, be, and

Sec. 6.02. - Classified and nonclassified service.

All offices and positions of the city shall either be in the nonclassified service
or in the classified service. The city manager and deputy city manager, city
attorney and deputy city attorney, city clerk and city auditor shall be
appointed by resolution of the city commission. Assistant city attorneys shall
be appointed by the city attorney. Commission assistants shall be appointed
by the City Commission. Assistant city clerks shall be appointed by the city
clerk and assistant city auditors shall be appointed by the city auditor. All
other nonclassified personnel shall be appointed by the city manager, who
shall be empowered to execute employment contracts with such
employees. The duration of such employment contracts shall not exceed
two (2) years, and the pay provisions shall be in conformance with the salary
range established in the city's pay ordinance. All positions in the classified
service shall be filled in accordance with personnel rules and regulations;
provided, however, that all positions in the classified service which, once
filled, are subject to the provisions of any collective bargaining agreement
shall be exempt from the applicability of such personnel rules and
regulations. Positions in the nonclassified service shall be filled on the basis

fair and equitable compensation, with incentives and recognition for
excellent performance. The nonclassified service shall include the following
positions and levels:

classified position except in accordance with personnel rules and
regulations.

measures.questionText: Should the City of Fort Lauderdale Charter be amended to establish the Charter position of Police Chief, who shall report directly to the City Commission rather than to the City Manager, and be employed and compensated under such terms and conditions as the City Commission deems appropriate?
measures.officialStatement:
(a) There is hereby established the position of Police Chief. The Police Chief shall be appointed by the City Commission and employed under such terms and conditions as the City Commission may deem appropriate. The Police Chief shall receive such compensation as the City Commission may by resolution fix and designate.

(b) The individual serving as Police Chief on the effective date of this section shall automatically become the first appointed Police Chief.

(c) The Police Chief shall reside in the City of Fort Lauderdale during his or her employment with the city, but he or she need not be a resident of the City of Fort Lauderdale or the State of Florida at the time of his or her appointment. Notwithstanding the foregoing sentence, the first appointed Police Chief need not reside in the City of Fort Lauderdale. Nor shall a Police Chief who is promoted to the position of Police Chief from within the Police Department need to reside in the City of Fort Lauderdale.

That this Ordinance shall be in full force and effect, as conditioned in Section 2,

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raises continuous permanent-residence requirements before qualifying from six to 12 months: city residence for mayor and district residence for commissioner, with an exception when redistricting moves a candidate’s permanent city residence into another district. Candidates must be U.S. citizens, registered city voters and provide at least five listed proofs of residency. The express 21-year minimum age would be removed. Candidates holding another elected office must file an irrevocable resignation at least ten days before qualifying begins and leave that office by the required handover date. City officers, workers and others serving the city cannot qualify, except incumbents seeking reelection or commissioners running for mayor. Officials must maintain the required residence or forfeit office. Certified elected officials would take office at the first regular Commission meeting after certification. The Commission would select a vice mayor at its first meeting after all elected officials take office, then annually, instead of each April. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the candidate-qualification and office-transition rules, including 12-month residency and five proofs, and the revised vice-mayor selection timing.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed changes to qualifications, taking office and vice-mayor selection.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires candidates for mayor or city commissioner to submit documents showing compliance with the Charter and applicable law to the City Clerk for an administrative review. It also revises the Charter wording on the Commission’s role in judging elections and member qualifications, which remains subject to court review. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the candidate-document submission and administrative-review procedure.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Removes the City Commission’s process for receiving a voter’s sworn allegation that a mayoral or Commission candidate violated the Charter or is unqualified, and for taking evidence and deciding that challenge. Such challenges would be considered by the courts. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve removing the Commission’s candidate-challenge process and leaving those questions to the courts.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject removal of the Commission’s candidate-challenge process.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increases the normal notice for a special City Commission meeting from six to 72 hours. For an emergency involving potential imminent harm to public health, safety or property, or a chance to lessen or avert a catastrophe, notice could be as much as practicable. The mayor or city manager would determine the emergency in consultation with the city attorney. The notice must state the meeting’s general purpose. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the 72-hour notice rule and the defined emergency exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed changes to special-meeting notice.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Resolves ties for the employee nominating committee in favor of employees with the longest continuous city service. The board certifying the employee-recommended Civil Service Board member would consist of the city manager’s designee and two members of the nominating committee, replacing the two city commissioners. It also removes the Civil Service Board’s duty to review job-class specifications and advise the city manager about them. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the seniority tie-breaker, revised election-board membership and removal of the job-class review duty.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed Civil Service Board changes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Distinguishes an interim city manager, selected by Commission resolution after resignation or removal, from an acting manager selected by the city manager during a temporary absence. An acting manager must be a deputy or assistant city manager or department director. An interim manager could be removed by Commission resolution without a public hearing. It also deletes obsolete primary-election references and repeals the Charter requirement for two newspaper publications for public hearings and other notices. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the manager-selection and terminology changes and removal of the specified primary-election and publication provisions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this group of proposed Charter changes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces the Charter’s competitive-bidding, public-notice and cash-sale rules for personal property with procedures set by ordinance. Sales of land to private parties, and exchanges or transfers to acquire property for a public improvement or use, would follow an ordinance and applicable law and need a four-commissioner resolution finding the transaction in the city’s best interest, subject to park-land rules. Transactions with other public bodies would need four votes and a purpose essential to city health, safety or welfare, even if a private party benefits incidentally. Covered private use agreements concern city land, including airspace, not needed for city purposes or used in a transaction acquiring property for a public improvement or use. Agreements longer than one year would require four votes. Terms over three and up to ten years would also need an independent fair-value and party-qualification review and a best-interest finding; terms over ten years would additionally need consideration of an independent business-viability report. The city hires the consultants at the private party’s expense. Renewals and extensions count toward the term. Assigning any covered agreement would require four votes. For a term over 50 years, the Charter initiative process could trigger a referendum to reject the agreement, with petitions signed by 15% of registered electors of the last election and the other initiative requirements met. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the revised property-transaction procedures, four-vote approvals and additional reviews for longer private use agreements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed changes to city property sales and use agreements.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Extends the requirement for a unanimous vote of the entire City Commission to licenses, concessions, facility-use agreements and other use agreements longer than one year for city land zoned Parks, Recreation and Open Space. Unanimous approval for sales, transfers and leases longer than one year would remain. The amendment also applies unanimous approval for removing the park zoning designation to all land with that designation, replacing the old limit to land zoned park on November 10,2004. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve requiring unanimous Commission approval for the additional park-land use agreements longer than one year.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject extending the unanimous-vote requirement to those park-land use agreements.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Makes police chief a Charter position appointed by and reporting directly to the City Commission, with employment terms and pay set by the Commission. The person serving as chief when the amendment takes effect would become the first appointee automatically. Chiefs must live in the city during employment, but may be appointed before becoming residents. The first appointee and chiefs promoted from within the Police Department are exempt from the city-residency requirement. The amendment would take effect ten days after certification of the election results.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve direct Commission appointment, oversight and compensation of the police chief, with the stated transition and residency exceptions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the proposed Charter police-chief position reporting to the Commission.
